title: docs-site feedback-driven edit-loop playbook
author: Marissa Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook describes the feedback-driven edit loop for the Redwood docs site. It covers the capture, triage, prioritization, authoring, review, release, and monitoring steps for user-facing documentation changes (SDK guides, API examples, quickstarts, and canonical fixes). The goal is to reduce mean time to fix (MTTFx) for high-impact doc issues while keeping the site stable for customers and internal users.

Goals
- Close actionable feedback within 72 hours for P1/P2 items.
- Deploy small, frequent doc fixes with automated validation.
- Maintain an observable backlog with owners and SLA targets.
- Ensure edits are tested locally and validated against snippet-runner and CI before merging.

Scope
- Included: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, canonical fixes surfaced from support, and docs-site operational procedures.
- Excluded: product design docs, private customer runbooks (use eng-private-deployments).

Roles & Responsibilities
- Docs Triage (rotating): capture and label incoming feedback, recommend priority and owner.
- Author (engineer or tech writer): implement content or code snippets, add tests.
- Reviewer (tech writer/engineer): check accuracy, tone, and linkages.
- Release Owner (docs infra): merge, bump site, monitor post-deploy telemetry.

Owner matrix (text table)
| Activity | Primary | Backup | Target SLA |
| Capture & label feedback | Docs Triage rotation | Support on-duty | 6 hours |
| Triage & prioritize | Docs Triage lead | Product manager | 24 hours |
| Author fix | Assigned author | Docs pool | 48 hours for P1/P2 |
| Review & approve | Tech writing team | Senior engineer | 24 hours |
| Merge & deploy | Release Owner | Docs infra lead | 2 hours post-merge |

Capture sources (where issues come from)
- In-product feedback widget (edge-case snippets and unexpected outputs).
- GitHub Issues opened by customers or engineers.
- Support tickets triaged into the docs backlog.
- Slack #docs-feedback and #support escalations.
- Automated snippet/runtime test failures (CI).

Priority guidelines
- P0: Security, legal, or doc content that causes data loss or directly misleads customers about security/compliance. Immediate response; stakeholders notified.
- P1: Incorrect API examples that break customer integrations, or misleading SDK usage. Target: fix and deploy in <72 hours.
- P2: Clarity/typo issues that cause confusion but have a workaround. Target: fix within 7 days.
- P3: Cosmetic or enhancement requests. Handled during regular editorial sprints.

Triage procedure (step-by-step)
1) Capture: Docs Triage engineer collects incoming items into the docs backlog board (Jira/GitHub Projects). Include reproduction steps, affected pages, and suggested fix.
2) Repro: If the feedback references a code snippet or example, attempt to reproduce locally using the docs snippet-runner. Add section "repro-steps" to the issue.
3) Assign priority and owner: Use priority guidelines. Assign an author or the docs pool.
4) Labeling: Add labels: area/<component>, priority/<P0|P1|P2|P3>, type/<bug|clarity|enhancement>, release-blocker if applicable.
5) Communicate: Post summary in #docs-triage with a direct @mention for the owner.

Authoring & Validation checklist
- Update the page Markdown or Confluence source in a feature branch.
- Run local preview: `yarn docs:dev` or `make preview`.
- Run snippet tests: `scripts/snippet-runner --filter <page-or-snippet>` (example below).
- Run unit linting: `yarn lint:md` and `yarn lint:code-snippets`.
- Add or update automated snippet tests under /tests/snippets/.
- Ensure examples use the canonical SDK patterns and do not rely on internal-only flags.

Code snippet: snippet-runner usage
```
# run all snippets for a single page
./scripts/snippet-runner --page "sdk/clients/python/quickstart.md"

# run a single snippet by id
./scripts/snippet-runner --snippet-id snippet-embed-032
```

CI & merge rules
- All PRs must pass: build, lint, snippet-runner, and preview smoke test.
- Small fixes (<= 10 lines of docs or single snippet change) may be merged by Docs Triage with one reviewer; larger changes require two reviewers including a tech writer.
- Use PR labels: `docs/fix`, `docs/enhancement`, `ci/needs-snippet-test`.

Example GitHub Actions job (YAML as text)
```
name: docs-ci
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install
        run: yarn install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Lint markdown
        run: yarn lint:md
      - name: Run snippet tests
        run: ./scripts/snippet-runner --ci
      - name: Build preview
        run: yarn build:preview
```

Release & deploy procedure
1) Merge PR to main following CI green.
2) Docs infra auto-builds preview and deploys to the staging canary environment.
3) Release Owner verifies that canonical pages render and critical snippets run in staging (smoke list below).
4) Promote to production via the release pipeline or wait for scheduled window (non-blocking P2/P3).

Smoke test checklist (post-deploy)
- Home page renders.
- SDK quickstart pages for Python and JS run snippet smoke tests.
- API reference crosslinks are intact.
- Search indexing includes the updated page.

Rollback & emergency fixes
- If a deploy introduces breakage (failed snippets, missing assets), execute rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/docs-site` (or use release pipeline rollback).
- For urgent P0/P1 fixes, follow the emergency change flow: 1) create minimal patch branch; 2) add `ci/skip-preview` only if preview build is known to be flaky; 3) get +1 from on-call release owner; 4) merge and force-promote to production; 5) notify customers and post incident note.

Communication templates
- Slack escalation (short):
  "[P1 DOCS] sdk/clients/python/quickstart.md breaks on snippet 'auth-setup' — reproduces locally. Assigned to @devpatel. Will patch today. Ticket: <link>"
- Release note blurb (for changelog):
  "docs: fix code example in Python quickstart to use token auth v2 — Marissa Chen (docs triage)"

Measuring success (metrics)
- Mean time to triage (target < 24 hrs).
- Mean time to production fix for P1 (target < 72 hrs).
- Post-deploy snippet failure rate (target < 0.5%).
- Customer-reported docs regressions per quarter (target decrease by 30% YoY).

Common support patterns and canonical fixes
- Broken SDK imports: prefer canonical import paths and pin to supported version in examples. Add a short code block that demonstrates correct imports and a quick troubleshooting note.
- Outdated API fields: include migration notes and back-compat samples.
- Rate limit/HTTP errors in examples: add explicit error handling snippet and link to rate-limits docs.

Editor & contribution conventions (quick list)
- Commit message format: `docs(scope): short description (#issue)`
- PR title: `docs: brief description of change` and include affected page links.
- Use final voice and second-person instructions for quickstarts.
- Include a short test-case in the PR description if a snippet reproduces the issue.

Appendix: example small-fix workflow (concise)
1) Create a branch `docs/fix/python-quickstart-auth-202602`
2) Update example and tests.
3) Run `./scripts/snippet-runner --snippet-id auth-setup` locally.
4) Open PR, add `docs/fix` label, request reviewer `@aisha`.
5) Merge when CI passes; Release Owner will promote.

Notes & references
